result:
Compiles cleanly on the first attempt.

I wrote `tests/com/google/gson/stream/JsonWriterAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 3.8 (`junit.framework.TestCase`) test class covering `JsonWriter`'s documented contract:

- **Fluent API**: every `begin*/end*/name/value/nullValue` returns `this`.
- **Structural encoding**: empty/nested arrays and objects, compact vs. indented output, exact JSON string assertions.
- **Value encoding**: `String` (incl. null → `null` literal), `jsonValue` (raw, unquoted), `nullValue`, `boolean`/`Boolean`, `double`/`Number` (finite values, and `IllegalArgumentException` for NaN/Infinite per "may not be NaNs or infinities"), `long` including `Long.MIN/MAX_VALUE` boundaries.
- **Lenient mode**: default `isLenient()==false`, strict mode rejecting top-level scalars/null (`IllegalStateException`), lenient mode permitting them and non-finite doubles.
- **Malformed-structure errors**: mismatched `endArray`/`endObject`, `name()` outside/inside wrong scope, missing `name()` before a value, consecutive `name()` calls, `name(null)` → `NullPointerException`, writing after a completed top-level document.
- **close()/flush()**: `IOException` on incomplete document close, success on complete document, and propagation of underlying `Writer` I/O failures (via a `FailingWriter` fixture).
- **htmlSafe**: default off leaves `< > & =` raw; enabling it strips all four raw characters from output.
- **serializeNulls**: default `true`, toggling it suppresses null object members but never affects array elements.
- An integration test mirroring the class-level javadoc example.

Ran only `./compile.sh` as instructed — did not execute the tests.
